name: Assegno Unico Universale - SIA Project 24 25
description:
Information Systems - academic year 24/25
Course Project

The Universal Single Allowance (Assegno Unico Universale, AUU) is a financial support for Italian families with dependent children, which guarantees financial aid based on the specific conditions and the age of the children. The AUU is paid by the National Social Security Institute (INPS) to those who exercise parental responsibility in the presence of children dependent on them.

The online application can be submitted to INPS either directly by the interested parties or by patronage institutes (patronati) holding a specific mandate. The application must be submitted on the INPS website, by subjects authenticated through one of the following options: SPID; Electronic Identity Card 3.0; National Services Card; PIN. The application can also be submitted from mobile devices and through the call center by calling the toll-free number 803.164 or the number 06 164 164. Here, only the case of submission of the application through the INPS website by the directly interested parties will be described (delegates are therefore excluded from the analysis).

A. APPLICATION ENTRY: PHASE 1 - USER DATA
It is possible to submit an application as:
- Parent;
- Custodial parent;
- Child's guardian.

Depending on the type of applicant, more or fewer fields must be filled in, according to the table below, and in the order in which they appear in the table.

| Field | Parent | Custodial parent | Child's guardian |
|---|---|---|---|
| Child's tax code | X | X | X |
| Declaration that the child is a dependent | X | X | X |
| Disabled child (yes/no) | X | X | X |
| If the child is disabled, degree of disability (Medium, Severe, Non-self-sufficiency) | X | X | X |
| Household (cohabiting parents; non-cohabiting parents; single parent) | X | | |
| Parent with sole custody (yes/no) | | X | |
| If the household is not single-parent, tax code of the other parent | X | X | |
| If the household is not single-parent, method of distribution of the allowance (50% or 100% to the applicant) | X | X | |

Also consider that:
- as soon as the applicant enters the child's tax code, it is verified immediately, in real time: if the child is present in other active applications, the application flow is blocked with an explanatory warning;
- upon submission of the application, in the absence of a valid ISEE already held by INPS, the allowance will be calculated with the minimum amount provided for by the regulations; should the ISEE be submitted to INPS at a later time, the user does not need to update their application: as soon as INPS comes into possession of the ISEE, the amount of the allowance is automatically recalculated.

The step that completes this phase is entering the tax codes of the dependent adult children, for whom it is not possible to request the single allowance but who contribute to determining the number of members of the household. If the tax code of an adult child is already present, an error is reported: the user can decide to try again or to move on to the next step, namely specifying the payment data.

B. APPLICATION ENTRY: PHASE 2 - PAYMENT DATA
When specifying the payment data, if in the previous phase the 50% distribution method with the other parent was declared, it will be required to also enter the payment data of the other parent. Otherwise, only one's own payment data must be entered. In both cases, one of the following payment methods can be chosen:
- credit to accounts with an IBAN, in the SEPA area, held in the name of the applicant and enabled to receive bank transfers (current account, savings book, prepaid card);
- domiciled bank transfer to the applicant at the post office counter;
- credit to a prepaid card for households receiving the Inclusion Income (Reddito di Inclusione).

C. APPLICATION ENTRY: PHASE 3 - DECLARATIONS AND SUBMISSION
The process ends with the reading of the declarations of responsibility and of the privacy notice (GDPR). Once the declarations of responsibility and the GDPR notice have been accepted, it is possible to view a summary of the data entered, useful for checking, before submitting the application, whether everything has been entered correctly. From the application summary it is possible to confirm everything in order to submit it. In case of an error (example: wrong IBAN entered), the application will not be submitted: an explicit error message is shown, the process ends and the user will have to reopen the application and modify the wrong fields. In case of no error, the application will be submitted and it will be possible to download the receipt.

D. APPLICATION VERIFICATION AND PAYMENTS
Once acquired, the application is analyzed by the staff of the competent Offices, who can decide whether to: reject it, because the applicant is not entitled to it; suspend it to request further documentation; accept it. In all cases, the system notifies the applicant. In case of acceptance, the application is valid for 12 months. The amount is paid on a monthly basis, and the payment takes place automatically. In case of suspension, see paragraph F.

E. CONSULTING AND COMPLETING A DRAFT APPLICATION
At any point of the application submission, it is possible either to abort the process without saving any data, or to save the application as a draft - if it has not yet been submitted - in order to continue entering the data at a later time using the dedicated functionality. The application can thus be consulted at any time. From the consultation it is possible to access the application completion functionality: after selecting “Complete”, the system asks whether one wants to continue editing: if this is confirmed (YES) it is possible to continue the submission of the previously saved application (in this case the user finds the data already entered previously). If instead it is not confirmed (NO) the previously saved data will be deleted and it will be possible to proceed with the entry starting from scratch.

F. ADDING ATTACHMENTS
If the application has been suspended to request further documents (see paragraph D), the notification also includes a message from the operator indicating the missing document(s). The user will then have to view their application and add the requested attachments. At the end of the addition, they will have to confirm again all the data present, and read and confirm the declarations of responsibility and the privacy notice.

G. COMPLETING THE APPLICATIONS SUBMITTED BY THE OTHER PARENT
Through this function it is possible to supplement the application filled in by the other parent. In this case one is not the applicant, i.e. the person who submits the application for the allowance, but the second parent. The main functionality that can be performed as the other parent, in addition to consulting the application data, is updating the payment method, i.e. it is possible to decide whether or not to confirm the allowance distribution requests made by the applicant. More precisely, if the applicant requests the allowance at 100%, as the other parent it is possible to confirm the request, by selecting “Paid 100% to the applicant”, otherwise it is possible not to confirm it by selecting “Distributed 50% between the parents”. If the request for the allowance at 100% is not confirmed, then one will have to enter one's own payment data. If, instead, the applicant requests the allowance at 50% for both parents, then it is possible to enter only the payment method. The process continues as described in paragraph C.

H. ADDING CHILDREN
It is possible to add one or more children to a pre-existing application. The data of the additional child(ren) are entered one at a time. In this case too, as soon as the applicant enters the child's tax code, it is verified immediately, in real time: if the child is present in other active applications, the application flow is blocked with an explanatory warning. Once the new data have been entered, the process continues as reported in paragraphs B and C: in this case, however, the data are already entered and it is possible to confirm or modify them.

I. FURTHER FUNCTIONALITIES
Finally, bear in mind that the system also makes the following operations possible for the citizen:
- Consult the submitted applications;
- Consult the general information on the single allowance for children;
- Simulate the amount of the monthly allowance.

Analysis
Analyze the scenario outlined above and define:
1. The conceptual information model (UML class diagram).
2. The process model (BPMN process diagram), with the exception of paragraph “I. FURTHER FUNCTIONALITIES”.
3. The use case model (UML UC diagram) at summary and user-goal level.
4. The narrative of the use cases at user-goal level identified in the previous point, with the exception of paragraph “I. FURTHER FUNCTIONALITIES”.
5. Evaluate advantages and disadvantages of developing a web system corresponding to the use cases described in point 4 by comparing two different alternatives (in both cases consider as a reference 250 working days per year, 8 working hours per day).
   a. The development is carried out by a team composed of 3 new hires (graduates in computer engineering for less than one year) and 1 senior project manager who has already coordinated a similar project. As for the new hires, consider that they will work the whole time exclusively on the AUU project and that they have a gross annual salary (RAL) of 35,000 euros. The senior, instead, will divide their time among 5 different projects (assume an equal distribution of time among projects), and with a RAL of 75,000 euros.
   b. A consulting company takes charge of the development, entrusting it to its own team of 5 developers with experience in similar systems. A senior analyst, she too with experience in similar systems, has been put in charge of the project. All 6 have been assigned to the project for half of their time, and the average cost per person of the team is 150 euros per day. In addition to these there is an INPS project manager who will follow the progress of the project: for her, consider a RAL of 80,000 euros and an occupation of her time of 5%.
highLevelGoals: The Applicant aims to successfully submit a complete and accurate application for the Universal Single Allowance to INPS, ensuring all necessary personal, child, and household data are provided.
The Applicant seeks to securely and correctly enter their preferred payment method and associated details (e.g., IBAN) to ensure timely and accurate receipt of the Universal Single Allowance.
The Applicant desires the ability to save an application in progress as a draft and return to complete it at a later time, avoiding the need to re-enter all data from scratch.
The Applicant wants to be able to view the current status and all relevant details of their previously submitted Universal Single Allowance applications.
The Applicant needs to be able to upload and attach any requested additional documents to a suspended application to facilitate its processing and approval.
The Applicant aims to update an active application by adding information for newly dependent children, ensuring the allowance calculation reflects the updated household composition.
The Applicant desires a tool to estimate the financial support they might receive, based on their family's specific conditions, before or during the application process.
The Other Parent needs to securely enter their payment information when the allowance is to be distributed 50% between both parents, as requested by the Applicant or chosen by the Other Parent.
The Other Parent aims to review and either confirm the Applicant's proposed allowance distribution (e.g., 100% to Applicant) or choose an alternative distribution (e.g., 50% to each parent).
The Other Parent seeks to view the details of an application submitted by the Applicant that pertains to their shared children, ensuring transparency and accuracy.
The INPS Staff aims to quickly and accurately review submitted applications for the Universal Single Allowance, determining eligibility and calculating the correct amount.
The INPS Staff needs to effectively notify applicants about the status of their application (accepted, rejected, suspended) and clearly communicate any requests for additional documentation.
The INPS Staff seeks to efficiently receive, store, and manage any supplementary documents provided by applicants for suspended applications.
The INPS Staff aims to guarantee that accepted applications result in correct monthly allowance payments being automatically disbursed to eligible families for the entire 12-month validity period.
lowLevelGoals: The Applicant will select a method (SPID, CIE, CNS, or PIN) and provide credentials to log into the system.
The Applicant will click a button or link to start a new application for the Universal Single Allowance.
The Applicant will input their personal identification details (e.g., name, surname, tax code) into the designated fields of the application form.
The Applicant will use an 'Add Child' function to input details for each dependent child (e.g., name, date of birth, tax code) into the application.
The Applicant will select an option to declare if a child is dependent for the purpose of the allowance.
The Applicant will select 'yes' or 'no' to indicate if a dependent child has a disability.
If a child is indicated as disabled, the Applicant will select the degree of disability from a predefined list.
The system will automatically check if the entered child's tax code is already associated with another active application during data entry.
The Applicant will receive a warning if a child's tax code is already in use and will be prompted to take appropriate action (e.g., confirm, correct, or remove).
The Applicant will select or input information regarding their household composition (e.g., marital status, cohabitation) as required by the application.
The Applicant will input the tax code of the other parent into the designated field if applicable.
The Applicant will choose how the allowance should be distributed (e.g., 100% to applicant, 50% to each parent).
The Applicant will access a summary page to review all entered data for accuracy before final submission.
The Applicant will read and explicitly accept the declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice before proceeding with the application submission.
The Applicant will click a 'Submit Application' button to send their complete application to INPS.
Upon successful submission, the Applicant will click a button to download a receipt of their application.
The Applicant will click a 'Cancel' or 'Exit' button to stop the application process without saving any entered data.
The Applicant will choose their preferred payment method (e.g., bank transfer, postal order) from a list of available options within the application.
The Applicant will input their International Bank Account Number (IBAN) into a dedicated field for direct deposit of the allowance.
The Applicant will review the entered payment details and confirm their accuracy before saving them.
The Applicant will click a 'Save Payment Details' button to store the provided payment information within their application.
The Applicant will click a 'Save Draft' button or similar option while filling out an application.
The Applicant will navigate to a section (e.g., 'My Drafts' or 'Incomplete Applications') to view all previously saved applications.
The Applicant will select a specific draft application from the list to continue filling out the form from where they left off.
When resuming a draft, the Applicant will choose 'NO' to continue editing, which will delete the current draft data and allow them to start a new application from scratch.
The Applicant will access a dedicated section (e.g., 'My Applications') to see a list of all their previously submitted Universal Single Allowance applications.
The Applicant will select an application from the list to view its current processing status (e.g., 'Submitted', 'In Review', 'Suspended', 'Accepted', 'Rejected').
The Applicant will access a detailed view of a selected application, including all personal, child, household, and payment data provided.
The Applicant will view their list of applications and identify those marked with a 'Suspended' status or a clear indication of 'Documents Required'.
The Applicant will click on a suspended application to open an interface specifically for uploading additional documents.
The Applicant will use a 'Browse' or 'Upload' button to select a file from their device and attach it to the suspended application.
After uploading documents, the Applicant will review and confirm all previously entered application data.
After uploading documents, the Applicant will read and explicitly accept the declarations of responsibility and the GDPR privacy notice again.
The Applicant will click a 'Submit Documents' button to finalize the upload of all requested additional documentation for the suspended application.
The Applicant will navigate to their list of active applications and choose one to update with new dependent child information.
The Applicant will locate and click an 'Add New Child' or similar button within the selected active application's details.
The Applicant will input all required information for the new dependent child (e.g., name, date of birth, tax code) into the provided fields.
The Applicant will click a 'Save Changes' or 'Update Application' button to incorporate the new child's details into the existing application.
The Applicant will click on a 'Simulate Allowance' or 'Estimate Amount' feature within the application portal.
The Applicant will enter details such as the number of dependent children, their ages, and any special conditions (e.g., disability) into the simulation tool.
The Applicant will input their ISEE value or select an option indicating their ISEE bracket for the allowance calculation simulation.
The Applicant will click a 'Calculate' or 'Simulate' button to generate an estimated monthly allowance amount based on the provided data.
The Applicant will see the estimated monthly allowance amount displayed on the screen after running the simulation.
The Other Parent will select a method (SPID, CIE, CNS, or PIN) and provide credentials to log into the system.
The Other Parent will navigate to a specific section in the portal to provide their payment information for shared allowance distribution.
The Other Parent will input their IBAN into the designated field to receive their share of the allowance.
The Other Parent will review and confirm the accuracy of their entered payment information before saving.
The Other Parent will click a 'Save Payment Details' button to store their IBAN for the 50% allowance distribution.
The Other Parent will navigate to a section (e.g., 'Allowance Distribution Requests') to view requests from the Applicant.
The Other Parent will view the details of the allowance distribution proposed by the Applicant (e.g., 100% to Applicant).
The Other Parent will click a 'Confirm' button to agree to the allowance distribution as proposed by the Applicant.
The Other Parent will choose a different distribution option (e.g., '50% to each parent') from a set of available choices.
The Other Parent will click a 'Submit' or 'Apply Changes' button to send their chosen allowance distribution to the system.
The Other Parent will navigate to a section (e.g., 'Applications by Other Parent') to view applications relevant to their shared children.
The Other Parent will select an application from the list to view its full details, including child information and household data.
The INPS Staff will log into the system and navigate to the 'Application Review' or 'Pending Applications' queue.
The INPS Staff will choose an application from the queue to begin the review process.
The INPS Staff will cross-reference the submitted personal, child, and household data with internal databases or external sources for accuracy.
The INPS Staff will apply predefined rules and criteria to determine if the applicant is eligible for the Universal Single Allowance.
The INPS Staff will use the system's calculation module to determine the correct monthly allowance amount based on verified data.
The system will automatically re-evaluate and update the allowance amount for applications initially processed with the minimum amount once the ISEE value becomes available.
The INPS Staff will select the 'Accept' option for an application that meets all eligibility criteria.
The INPS Staff will select the 'Reject' option for an application that does not meet eligibility criteria, providing a reason.
The INPS Staff will select the 'Suspend' option and specify which additional documents are required from the applicant.
The INPS Staff will trigger the system to send an automated notification to the applicant confirming their application has been accepted.
The INPS Staff will trigger the system to send an automated notification to the applicant informing them of the rejection and the reason.
The INPS Staff will trigger the system to send an automated notification to the applicant stating their application is suspended and listing the required additional documents.
The INPS Staff will navigate to a specific module designed to handle additional documents for suspended applications.
The INPS Staff will open a suspended application to see a list of documents recently uploaded by the applicant.
The INPS Staff will open and examine each uploaded document to ensure it meets the requirements and is valid.
The INPS Staff will update the status of each reviewed document within the system.
The INPS Staff will trigger a scheduled or manual process to initiate monthly allowance payments for all accepted applications.
The INPS Staff will ensure that all accepted applications have valid and complete payment information (e.g., IBAN) before payment disbursement.
The INPS Staff will use a dashboard or report to track the success and status of all monthly allowance payments.
The INPS Staff will investigate and resolve any issues related to failed or rejected monthly allowance payments.
The system will automatically process and disburse monthly allowance payments to eligible applicants based on their provided payment details.
